In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the non physicians in this study identified specific areas of knowledge gaps and physician behaviors that could be targets for medical education interventions designed to improve interprofessional collaboration.

non physician healthcare professionals identified knowledge gaps as barriers to collaboration with resident physicians, and that physician behaviors such as mutual support and good communication contributed to good collaborative relationships.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most important aspect to improving collaboration between physicians and non-physician healthcare professionals is mutual respect.
non physicians are willing to collaborate with physicians but that they would like physicians to better understand the roles and processes of other healthcare professionals.
the non-physician team members identified that they wanted to be treated as equals and have their input valued.
The main takeaway from our work is that
non physician healthcare professionals are eager to collaborate with physicians, but that physicians' behaviors can make or break the relationship.
the AAMC should not assume that physicians are automatically able to collaborate effectively with non physicians.
medical educators must include non physician voices in discussions regarding how to best teach interprofessional collaboration.
